---
title: "Simulating a simple resilience threshold"
description: "A minimal agent-based model shows how small perturbations can flip a stable population into collapse."
date: "2026-08-10"
---

This is an example note — replace it with your own. It shows the kind of
thing this setup is good for: real Python code, run at render time, sitting
next to the explanation.

We simulate a population under a simple logistic growth rule with an added
stress term, and sweep the stress parameter to find where the population
stops recovering.

```{python}
#| label: fig-collapse
#| fig-cap: "Population trajectories under increasing stress. Placeholder model — replace with your own."

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def simulate(stress, steps=60, r=0.35, K=100, x0=80):
    x = np.zeros(steps)
    x[0] = x0
    for t in range(1, steps):
        growth = r * x[t-1] * (1 - x[t-1] / K)
        x[t] = max(x[t-1] + growth - stress, 0)
    return x

ink, teal, rust, moss, line = "#1E2A24", "#2B5F5A", "#A6532A", "#6B7B4F", "#D9D2BE"
stresses = [1, 4, 7]
colors = [teal, moss, rust]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 3.4))
fig.patch.set_alpha(0)
ax.set_facecolor("none")

for s, c in zip(stresses, colors):
    ax.plot(simulate(s), color=c, linewidth=2, label=f"stress = {s}")

ax.set_xlabel("Time step", color=ink, fontsize=9)
ax.set_ylabel("Population", color=ink, fontsize=9)
ax.tick_params(colors=ink, labelsize=9)
for spine in ["top", "right"]:
    ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)
for spine in ["left", "bottom"]:
    ax.spines[spine].set_color(line)
ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=9, labelcolor=ink)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

At low stress the population settles into a stable equilibrium. Past a
threshold, it can't recover fast enough between shocks and collapses to
zero — the same qualitative behavior discussed on the [Research](/research.qmd)
page, here in a model simple enough to fit in one code block.
